correctness.rationale: Checked the unnormalized directed-edge convention and the same-tail/head predecessor/successor counts. They give K=XWX^T−YWY^T with W=diag(d−2). An independent rank derivation uses orthonormal symmetric/antisymmetric vectors for each pair of arcs: K has zero diagonal blocks and off-diagonal block SWD^T, where S and D here are the unoriented and signed edge-by-vertex incidences. Connectivity gives im D^T=1^perp. The kernel of S is zero if nonbipartite and otherwise spanned by the bipartition sign b. Thus the block has rank n−1 except when b belongs to W(1^perp), precisely when 1^T W^(−1)b=0; then it has rank n−2. Block singular values give both signs. Independently checked the inverse-form radical argument in the record and the trace-square formula by X^TX=Y^TY=diag(d), X^TY=A. For the regular spectrum, each adjacency eigenvector at |lambda|<d generates a two-dimensional plane with the stated ± eigenvalues. At |lambda|=d, the overlap gives a one-dimensional common subspace, not a two-dimensional plane. If k is the count of these exceptional adjacency eigenvalues, that subspace contributes k zeros and the orthogonal complement contributes 2m−2n+k, yielding the stated 2m−2n+2k total. This clarifies the source's abbreviated attribution of zeros without changing its formula. Frozen script inspected only; its reported finite output is not the basis of acceptance.
residual_risks: No extension to degree-two vertices, for which W may be singular; no independent finite program run was needed.

value.rationale: The self-commutator measures nonnormality of a standard graph operator. The result determines its full signed rank profile in terms of elementary graph data, revealing an extra nullity jump among irregular bipartite graphs that regular formulas and bipartiteness alone miss. The balance test is operational without forming a 2m-by-2m matrix and distinguishes K_{3,4} from the balanced irregular K_{4,4} minus an edge. This structural payoff does not rely on treating the regular corollary as novel.
residual_risks: Does not determine magnitudes of the irregular eigenvalues or make a general normalized-operator claim.
